old: Read this slowly into a recorder, speak it aloud, or learn its movement and use silent words if that comes easily. Choose one anchor—a sound, bodily contact, or your two-hand practice—and an opening phrase. Keep using the same anchor where the words refer to it. Pause between paragraphs; don’t read the delivery directions aloud.
new: Practise how you are going to read this script into the recorder. It may be that you will read it slowly, or it may be that you will read it aloud, or it may be that you will learn it and say the words silently to yourself. Decide which of the three anchors you will use throughout – either the sound, or the bodily contact, or the two hands held together. Decide which opening words you will use. So whenever you see the word ‘anchor’ in the script below, you use the one you have chosen. At the end of each paragraph you pause for a few moments. Do not read aloud the instructions about how to read it.

old: Let your eyes settle somewhere in the room, somewhere they can rest for a little while, and notice the difference between looking for something and letting what is already there come into view.
new: Just to look somewhere in the room. Let your eyes rest for a moment on something. Just noticing what you see. There’s a big difference between looking for something and seeing what’s already there.

old: There is a surface beneath you. Notice where you meet it … the contact, the pressure, whatever you can actually feel. And while you notice that, a sound may reach you, or a breath may draw your attention, without needing you to arrange either one.
new: While you’re noticing something on a surface in front of you, see if you can notice something else at the same time. Perhaps what you’re sitting on and how it feels to be in contact with it. Then let something take your attention – perhaps a sound or even your own breathing.

old: You can give this a little time.
new: Is there time for you to do this?

old: A thought about the day may still be here. A thought about whether you’re doing this properly may be here too. There is room to notice a thought and return to the anchor you chose, without finishing the thought first.
new: See if there’s a thought there, it may be a thought about something that happened during the day, or it may be a thought about how you should be doing this. See if you can bring your attention back to the anchor, even if there is a thought there.

old: And as you return, you may find one detail that holds your interest … something about the sound, or the contact, or that particular way of listening … and let attention stay with it long enough to become curious.
new: And when you do come back, just look for something that holds your interest for a moment. It might be something you hear, someone you’re in contact with, or how you are listening.

old: Perhaps you can give yourself the time you would give someone you care about who has begun to speak and hasn’t yet found the words. You can remain nearby, listening, without finishing their sentence for them.
new: Perhaps you can be patient with yourself, in the same way that you might be patient with someone you love who is trying to tell you something.

old: Let your chosen phrase come to mind now. Say it as an invitation, and notice how it is received.
new: Take the phrase you have chosen and let it come to mind. Perhaps say it as an invitation and feel how it is received.

old: As you continue, your eyes can close, soften, or stay open. Let that be a choice you make. Listening may deepen while a sound from the room remains available in the background.
new: You may close your eyes, soften them, or continue with them open. Perhaps allow yourself to listen more deeply to what is happening for you, allowing some of what is happening in the room as background to your exploration.

old: Count slowly from five to one. Give each number its own moment.
new: Take a moment and count slowly from 5 to 1.

old: Five. Notice your chosen anchor again. Four. Let attention gather around what you find. Three. Leave a little space after the words. Two. Listen into that space, without preparing an answer. One. Stay here for a moment.
new: 5 As you do this, perhaps you can notice the thing you decided on to be your anchor for today. 4. Notice it 3. and after you have said a few words about it, leave some space 2. Just listen into that space, don’t prepare anything 1. Just stay here for a moment.

old: Bring your chosen concern lightly to mind, or remain with your wish for contact. Let it be present without rehearsing its whole story.
new: Bring to mind, lightly, the thing you have chosen to be concerned about, or simply your wish to contact.

old: Give the response time to take its own form. It might be a sensation, a few words, an image, a feeling, or an impulse to move. There may be nothing clear yet.
new: (Allow yourself time to notice what you notice. It may take the form of sensations, words, images, feelings, or a desire to move, or it may not yet be clear.)

old: Leave room to notice, with words or without them.
new: (Allow yourself time to notice this, with or without words.)
